solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pressure put on skilled worker, resistance fighter

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it, so the pressure letter goes on top

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for pressure in physics
an artisan is a craftsman, a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: A tradesman under pressure turns out to be a member of the resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a member of an armed group fighting covertly against an occupying force, a resistance fighter.

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the expert comes after the soldiers

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for soldiers, as in officers and men
an ace is an expert, someone highly skilled

explanation.surface: A skilled operative chases troops who are in peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a threat or source of harm, a synonym of danger.

parts.note: ate is the past tense of eat, to take food

explanation.surface: A man ate a meal with his companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is an informal British synonym for a pal or companion.

clue.text: Think logically with reference to a male child

parts.note: re is a formal word meaning concerning or with reference to
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to use their head where a boy is concerned.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to think in a logical, ordered way, drawing conclusions from facts.

clue.text: A cold potato dish initially caused a puzzle

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
rosti is a Swiss dish of fried grated potato

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the word caused

explanation.surface: A chilled potato dish set someone a problem to solve.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrostic is a word puzzle in which the first letters of lines spell out a word.

indicators.note: not says the letter for right is to be left out of the word for standing

parts.note: stature means standing or reputation, as in a person of some stature

explanation.surface: A figure stands in a fixed pose, but something about it is not right.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, often cast in bronze from a mould.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
in Britain sweet is a dessert, and pud is short for pudding, another word for dessert

explanation.surface: A small sweet potato is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet potato' looks like one vegetable, but 'sweet' is the dessert and 'potato' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is an informal word for a potato.

parts.note: to aver is to maintain or assert something as true
age can mean maturity, as in coming of age

explanation.surface: Someone intends to keep their grown-up composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as a verb meaning intend, but it is the noun for an arithmetic middle value.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of numbers is its average, the sum divided by the count.

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub them by ignoring them
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student is badly upset after being ignored on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut up is a British idiom for being very upset or grief-stricken.

clue.text: One article about another clan chief

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first article goes round the second

parts.note: the is one of the articles, the definite one
another article here is an, the indefinite one

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a second one concerns the head of a clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, but it means the grammatical words the and an.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was a Scottish nobleman heading a clan, as Macbeth was Thane of Cawdor.

indicators.note: first in says take the opening letter of the word series

parts.note: potted means condensed or abridged, as in a potted history

explanation.surface: Someone watched the opening episode of a series in shortened form.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted is a past-tense synonym of saw, meaning noticed or caught sight of.

clue.text: Let ponies loose? Make a decision tomorrow

indicators.note: loose suggests the letters are set free and scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Should the ponies be freed? Someone puts off the decision until morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to delay deciding until after a night's rest, so the choice is made the next day.

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: half of says take the first half of the letters of spectators

explanation.surface: A vantage point is reserved for half the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide view of a landscape, as from a hilltop.

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words novel and Kidnapped, across the break

explanation.surface: An animal appears in Kidnapped, Stevenson's adventure novel.
explanation.definitionFit: An elk is a large deer, so it is a creature.

parts.note: keys are things that open locks
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: Openers in a sound state create a base for building.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central principle on which something rests, its foundation.

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor

explanation.surface: Police detain a seaman from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Nab is an informal verb for catching or arresting someone.

clue.text: Clever, supporter wearing latest in grey

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment

indicators.note: latest means the final letter of the word grey

explanation.surface: A clever person wears a grey bra.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainy is an informal adjective for intelligent or clever.

clue.text: Concerned with smell round large mill

parts.note: O is round in shape
a mill is a factory, as in a cotton mill

explanation.surface: Someone is bothered by the stench around a big mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Olfactory is the adjective relating to the sense of smell.

clue.text: A line in very good last act

indicators.note: in says the A and the line letter go inside the word for very good

parts.note: fine means very good, excellent

explanation.surface: A single line in an excellent closing act of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing part of a show or piece of music, its last act.

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the words Dartmoor, a Tory

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician from Dartmoor addresses the public.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a moorland area in Devon, England; a Tory is a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a public speaker, especially a skilled one.

parts.note: a play is a drama
PE, physical education, is training at school
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Drama and fitness training for a knight in a fenced area.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a small portable enclosure where a baby can play safely.

clue.text: Feel sorry for mine, and yours at first

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: at first says take the opening letter of the word yours

explanation.surface: Someone sympathises with my situation and with yours first.
explanation.definitionFit: To pity someone is to feel sorrow or compassion for them.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the talk word goes round the king letter

parts.note: chat means talk
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A discussion about the monarch's scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart is a map or diagram, and to chart a course is to plan it.

clue.text: Caught, bird of prey in hood

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an owl is a nocturnal bird of prey

explanation.surface: A hawk or similar raptor is trapped wearing a hood.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a large loose hood, as worn by monks.

clue.text: At home, confined to bed, rejected pick-me-up

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the combined letters are read backwards
confined to says the home word is held inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone stuck at home in bed refused a restorative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' reads as part of the scene, but it gives IN; 'confined to' and 'rejected' then work on CINOT, the home word held in the bed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a restorative medicine or drink taken to boost energy.

definitions.meaning: the ... is the inside information or relevant facts
... as an adjective means base, mean or dishonourable

explanation.surface: Intelligence is sought about something contemptible.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is the true facts; as an adjective it is despicable.
